The 2021 report's own methodology section states: 'The model is set up in a way similar to that in an earlier study by the authors using the commercial power system modelling platform, PLEXOS (PEG, 2019) (Dukkipati, Dixit, Gambhir, & Chitnis, 2019)...The earlier PLEXOS model is modified with the same inputs as the GridPath model, and the results from both these models are compared. exact_snippet_or_quote: OCCTO: Shared a case study where PLEXOS is utilized to evaluate grid congestion and security of supply while integrating renewable energy into the power system.
why_it_supports_the_claim: REVERSES prior rejection ORG-ASIA-0003. OCCTO's own committee materials (occto.or.jp, 調整力及び需給バランス評価等に関する委員会, meetings #25/2018, #42/2019, #102/2024, #109/2025) are a first-person primary source in which OCCTO states in its own words ('当機関は...PLEXOSを活用した供給信頼度評価モデルについて検討を進めている' / 'our organization is proceeding with examination of a PLEXOS-based supply reliability evaluation model') that it has been building and technically evaluating PLEXOS models for its own supply-reliability (EUE/LOLE) assessment methodology since at least 2018, most recently reported 2025. This is categorically different from and far stronger than both (a) the original rejection evidence (OCCTO named only as a public data source in an Energy Exemplar Asia-Pacific Gas dataset brochure) and (b) the Xcelerate Japan 2024 vendor session title evidence (ORG-XCELM-0005, 'PLEXOS User Case Study Presentation - OCCTO', speaker Yu Takatsuji, General Planning Department, OCCTO) which itself is corroborated and superseded by this primary source. Classified as direct_user on the strength of OCCTO's own multi-year, first-person, self-published technical record of actively building and running PLEXOS models, which meets the catalogue's bar for 'organization itself operates PLEXOS' even though full tool migration is undecided.

source_title: Hawai’I Asia pacific Regional Energy System Assessment (APRESA)  ASEAN Interconnection Masterplan Study (AIMS) III Support
exact_snippet_or_quote: HNEI GridSTART provided training to the ASEAN Center for Energy (ACE), an intergovernmental organization within the ASEAN structure representing the AMS interests in the energy sector, on production cost analysis and use of the PLEXOS software tool to empower ACE personnel to more effectively carry out project management duties for the AIMS III study.
why_it_supports_the_claim: DEDICATED FOLLOW-UP per unresolved_questions.md batch63_regional_subject flag: investigated ACE itself (Jakarta-based ASEAN intergovernmental secretariat), not the ASEAN member states, as a direct_user/commissioner candidate for the AIMS III regional PLEXOS study. ACE's own AIMS III Phase 1&2 Report states 'The Head of the ASEAN Power Utilities/Authorities (HAPUA) Council appointed the ASEAN Centre for Energy (ACE) as the Implementing Agency (IA)' and 'The AIMS III Report was jointly developed by ACE and the national experts from the ASEAN Member States as part of the AIMS III Working Group, with GE Energy Consulting and Consortium as the consultant' [2]. 'The capacity expansion planning task was made with PLEXOS using Energy Exemplar as the simulation tool' [2] -- confirming PLEXOS as the actual tool used to build the AIMS III capacity-expansion model. ACE's own news page independently corroborates that ACE selected and directed GE Energy Consulting as the PLEXOS-running consultant: 'ACE with its selected consultant to lead the works of AIMS III, GE Consortium, wisely welcomed the inputs and feedbacks from all TRG members' [3]. HNEI/GridSTART's own project page confirms ACE itself received hands-on PLEXOS training, but frames it as management-oversight capacity rather than production modeling: 'HNEI GridSTART provided training to the ASEAN Center for Energy (ACE)...on production cost analysis and use of the PLEXOS software tool to empower ACE personnel to more effectively carry out project management duties for the AIMS III study' [1]. ROLE JUDGMENT (8-question evaluator checklist applied): (1) Is PLEXOS named? Yes, explicitly and repeatedly in ACE's own report. (2) Is the org named as doing something specific with it? Yes -- ACE is named as the appointing/directing Implementing Agency that selected and managed the PLEXOS-running consultant (GE Energy Consulting), and procured PLEXOS-proficiency from that consultant via its own RFP (per unresolved_questions.md's prior citation of ACE's 2018 RfP language). (3) Did ACE itself build/operate the production PLEXOS model? No -- the report attributes the actual capacity-expansion PLEXOS simulation work to 'GE Energy Consulting and Consortium as the consultant', not to ACE directly; the PLEXOS training ACE personnel received is explicitly scoped to 'project management duties' (i.e. overseeing/reviewing the consultant's work), not independently running production AIMS III simulations. (4) Therefore commissioner (procuring/directing party), not direct_user, is the correct role -- parallel to the ARENA/NERA (ORG-0004) and Energy Community Secretariat/EIHP (ORG-EEUR-0017) precedents already in the master catalogue, where the commissioning body is distinguished from the consultant who actually runs PLEXOS. (5) Second independent evaluator check: the alternative reading (ACE as direct_user, since ACE personnel underwent PLEXOS-specific training and ACE is listed as joint-developer/author of the Report) was considered and rejected because no source states ACE personnel ran the production capacity-expansion/production-cost simulations themselves -- training for 'project management duties' is explicitly narrower than running the model, consistent with the catalogue's qa_reviewer/commissioner distinction elsewhere (cf. EPPEI/ORG-ASIA-0017). (6) Not a duplicate: ACE itself has no prior row in the master catalogue; the only prior ASEAN/AIMS III row (INVESTIGATED-REG-0005) was a REJECTED subject_of_study candidate for the member states collectively, a different organization and a different role question, per this task's explicit framing. (7) Country recorded as Indonesia, ACE's HQ/domicile (Jakarta), consistent with the catalogue convention of recording the commissioning organization's own home country rather than the regional scope of its study. (8) Current: ACE continues in this Implementing Agency/Regional Planning Coordinator role into AIMS III Phase 3 (2024-2025 ASEAN-wide IRRP work), per a 2025 ACE-authored report proposing ACE take on an expanded role as 'custodian of the regional IRRP model' (not independently cited here as PLEXOS-specific evidence since that document describes Phase 3 methodology/governance, not confirmed current PLEXOS operation -- flagged below for future monitoring). NEW organization for the master catalogue.

A corroborating World Bank Contract-Awards-in-IPF (STEP) record (ledger id 2) confirms supplier of record ENERGY EXEMPLAR (EUROPE) LIMITED, award amount USD 148,622, FY2023, method Direct Selection, review type Post, location 'Western and Central Africa, Benin'. ICC = the WAPP Information and Coordination Centre, the West African Power Pool's regional system and market operator (Secretariat department), physically headquartered in Cotonou, Benin ('The WAPP Secretariat General is established in Cotonou, Benin' -- WAPP's own EuropeAid prior-information notice and WAPP ToR documents; RTE International's own case study independently confirms 'Technical assistance for the WAPP's Information and Coordination Centre... Country: Benin'). CLASSIFICATION: direct_user -- WAPP/ICC is the Borrower-side acquiring/operating entity procuring its OWN PLEXOS license to run regional system planning and market operations, not a vendor marketing case study and not a passive subject of someone else's model. PLEXOS: Integrated Energy Model v7.3'). Country recorded as Benin because that is where WAPP's Secretariat/ICC is physically headquartered and where the Borrower contract reference (BJ- prefix = Benin ISO code in WAPP/World Bank contract numbering) is filed; the organization's institutional remit is the full 14-country WAPP membership (Benin, Cote d'Ivoire, Burkina Faso, Ghana, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Togo) -- flagged in unresolved_questions.md for the same multi-country-field convention question already raised for ORG-NWAFR-0003/0004. why_it_supports_the_claim: Mott MacDonald, engaged by Barbados' Ministry of Energy, Small Business and Entrepreneurship (MESBE) and funded by the Inter-American Development Bank (IADB), built and ran a PLEXOS model of Barbados' entire power system for the country's Integrated Resource and Resiliency Plan (IRRP). Mott MacDonald's own project page states in first-person voice: 'We built a simulation of the entire energy system of Barbados, to explore different ways in which the government could approach its energy transition. To build the digital twin, we used the PLEXOS energy market simulation software platform (licensed by Energy Exemplar), and included inputs for generation, transmission, demand and many other variables.' The companion IRRP Activity B Draft Report (22 June 2021, energy.gov.bb, ledger id 2) corroborates with a glossary entry: 'PLEXOS Energy system simulation and optimisation software licensed by Energy Exemplar and industry standard software for energy system planning, simulation, and optimisation.' Project scope ran generation and transmission planning studies 2021-2031 (per the project page) producing three decarbonisation scenarios. Current: no evidence found this pass that the engagement has ended; the IRRP report itself is dated 2021-2024 (final report referenced on energy.gov.bb as of October 2024 upload) and is described as an ongoing framework for current/future Barbados governments. exact_snippet_or_quote: Hawaiian Electric proposes to use the RESOLVE model to produce a reference optimized resource plan that is then verified in PLEXOS through an hourly production simulation to capture total system costs as part of the Grid Needs Assessment.

why_it_supports_the_claim: Surfaced as a direct consequence of investigating ACE's AIMS III engagement (ORG-ACEASEAN-0001): ACE's own AIMS III Phase 1&2 Report names 'GE Energy Consulting and Consortium as the consultant' engaged (under ACE's direction, per HAPUA's appointment of ACE as Implementing Agency) to jointly develop the AIMS III Report with ACE and AMS national experts [2], and states 'The capacity expansion planning task was made with PLEXOS using Energy Exemplar as the simulation tool' [2] in the methodology section describing GE Energy Consulting's work. ACE's own news coverage of the 2nd Technical Review Group Meeting (March 2020) independently corroborates GE Energy Consulting's role as the named lead consultant: 'ACE with its selected consultant to lead the works of AIMS III, GE Consortium, wisely welcomed the inputs and feedbacks from all TRG members' [3]. Classified consultant_modeler (not commissioner or direct_user) because GE Energy Consulting is the party that actually built and ran the PLEXOS capacity-expansion simulations on ACE/HAPUA's behalf, parallel to the MMA/Transpower (ORG-NZERCOT-0002) and EIHP/Energy Community Secretariat (ORG-EEUR-0016) consultant_modeler precedents already in the master catalogue. Country recorded as United States (GE Energy Consulting's own corporate home, a General Electric energy-consulting division headquartered in the US) per the established convention of recording the consulting firm's own domicile rather than the client's region (cf. MMA/Australia precedent, ORG-NZERCOT-0002). why_it_supports_the_claim: IRENA's 2025 'Regional Energy Transition Outlook: South America' report acknowledgements state (verbatim): 'The authors wish to thank the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) for its support in facilitating the power sector modelling of the region in PLEXOS, Juan Roberto Paredes (IDB) for the assistance in engagement activities and report review, and Frank Leañez (consultant) for the South American countries' analysis.' IDB is a distinct organization from IRENA (already catalogued as ORG-VMINE-0031) and is credited specifically with facilitating the PLEXOS power-sector modelling underlying this regional study, which covers continental South America including the gap_confirmed countries Bolivia, Paraguay, Uruguay, Ecuador and Venezuela, plus Colombia. Role classified commissioner (facilitating/funding-adjacent role in enabling the PLEXOS modelling) rather than direct_user since the named consultant (Frank Leañez), not IDB staff directly, performed the PLEXOS runs. Flagged for a second-pass role review per AGENT_DESIGN_SPEC Section F since the commissioner vs. direct_user distinction here is a judgment call based on an acknowledgements paragraph rather than a methods section. Corroborates the commissioner classification -- IDB provided/owns the starting-point model from a prior IDB study, cross-verified against IDB's own 2017 publication; the 2025 PLEXOS analysis itself was performed by named external consultant Frank Leanez. Role classification upheld as commissioner.

institution_name: Southern California Gas Company (SoCalGas) and San Diego Gas & Electric Company (SDG&E)
use_case: Runs a PLEXOS production cost model that simulates hourly least-cost dispatch of Western US generation to forecast natural gas demand from utility electric generation (UEG) customers in its California Cost Allocation Proceeding (CAP) applications (2027-2029 CAP period).
source_title: Prepared Direct Testimony of R. Fiola M. Michelle Dandridge on Behalf of SoCalGas and SDG&E (Large Electric Generation/Cogen Forecast), CAP Application A.25-09-XXX
exact_snippet_or_quote: This forecast uses the PLEXOS model (Model) developed by the software provider Energy Exemplar, Inc. The Model evaluates, in detail, the least-cost dispatch of the electricity supply to meet system demand on an hourly basis and provides results of generation unit output, including fuel burn.
why_it_supports_the_claim: First-party regulatory testimony by SoCalGas/SDG&E staff explicitly names PLEXOS (by Energy Exemplar) as the production cost model used to build their UEG natural gas demand forecast for the CAP proceeding.
notes: Evidence from search snippet of the utility's own direct testimony; PDF not downloaded. PLEXOS is used for gas-demand forecasting from electric-plant dispatch, not for electric resource planning. Same method used in the 2024-2027 CAP (testimony of Jeff Huang, socalgas.com) and prior California Gas Reports, so usage is longstanding. SDG&E is a PG&E Corp affiliate; row covers the joint filing.
summary: Used PLEXOS to simulate hourly least-cost dispatch of Western US generation to forecast natural gas demand for its California Cost Allocation Proceeding applications.

use_case: ORNL researchers used PyPSA (version 0.24.0) as the power network solver, coupled with EPANET for water, to simulate network rebalancing following transmission line outages in a cascading-failure study of synthetic power and water networks for the City of Phoenix.
source_title: Cascading Failure Propagation and Perfect Storms in Interdependent Infrastructures
exact_snippet_or_quote: Using the City of Phoenix as a case study, synthetic power and water networks are constructed and coupled, and disturbances are simulated to capture cascading failure behaviors within and across power and water distribution systems. Network solvers [PyPSA (version 0.24.0) for power and EPANET (version 2.2) for water] are used to capture network rebalancing. Failures are simulated starting with transmission line outages and 120,000 simulations used to capture stochasticity in the rebalancing of power and water systems.
why_it_supports_the_claim: ORNL's own publication page states that PyPSA version 0.24.0 was used as the power network solver in their cascading-failure simulation work.
notes: First-party evidence from ORNL's publication page (snippet verbatim). Study uses a synthetic Phoenix power/water network as case study, so usage is for research simulation rather than an operational planning product. ORNL also appears in this catalogue's PLEXOS rows; this is a separate PyPSA finding.
summary: Used PyPSA in research to simulate network rebalancing after transmission line outages in a cascading-failure study of the City of Phoenix.

use_case: Stanford Department of Energy Resources Engineering researchers (Tehranchi, Barnes, Frysztacki, Azevedo) built PyPSA-USA, an open-source framework for power system planning and capacity expansion analysis in the continental United States, built on the PyPSA framework, including transmission expansion studies under decarbonization pathways.
source_title: PyPSA-USA: A flexible open-source energy system model and optimization tool for the United States
exact_snippet_or_quote: PyPSA-USA: A flexible open-source energy system model and optimization tool for the United States by Kamran Tehranchi, Trevor Barnes, Martha Frysztacki, Ines Azevedo ... In this paper, we introduce PyPSA-USA, a novel, flexible, open-source model framework designed for power system planning in the continental United States. Built on the Python for Power System Analysis (PyPSA) framework, PyPSA-USA is highly configurable to support system operations and planning research at variable spatial and temporal scales.
why_it_supports_the_claim: The paper's author affiliations list Stanford University (and SFU/KIT), and the abstract states the tool is built on the PyPSA framework for US power system planning, directly evidencing Stanford as a first-party research user/builder.
notes: First-party authorship: PyPSA-USA is developed and maintained by the Stanford team (pypsa-usa.readthedocs.io is their documentation; the docs also reference CPUC/CAISO data for their California configuration). Stanford already has a PLEXOS row in the catalogue; this is the separate PyPSA finding. Evidence is the SSRN abstract-page snippet; full PDF not downloaded. Also found as: NA-D2-0042.
summary: Used PyPSA in research to build PyPSA-USA for power system planning and transmission expansion studies under decarbonization pathways in the continental United States.

use_case: PJM uses PROMOD IV as its primary software for Market Efficiency analysis within the Regional Transmission Expansion Plan (RTEP), simulating hourly security-constrained commitment and dispatch for years 2025, 2029, 2032 and 2035 (with 2039 validation runs) to determine the economic benefits of transmission projects.
source_title: 2024/2025 Market Efficiency Input Assumptions - Mid-Cycle Update (TEAC informational item, January 2025)
exact_snippet_or_quote: The primary analytical software used by PJM to determine potential Market Efficiency benefits is PROMOD IV from Hitachi Energy. PROMOD IV is a production costing software application that simulates the hourly commitment and dispatch of generation to meet input load while recognizing and maintaining transmission system security limits.
why_it_supports_the_claim: This is PJM's own committee document explicitly naming PROMOD IV as the primary software for its RTEP Market Efficiency simulations.
notes: First-party PJM TEAC committee document (snippet from search result; underlying PDF not separately fetched per session rules). Corroborated by PJM's own 2017 'PJM PROMOD Overview' deck (https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/committees-groups/subcommittees/cs/20170811/20170811-item-02-pjm-promod-overview.ashx): 'PROMOD analysis is a critical component of the PJM Regional Transmission Expansion Process (RTEP)'. PJM is already in the catalogue as a PLEXOS user; this is a separate PROMOD record. Also found as: NA-D2-0060.
summary: Used PROMOD IV to simulate hourly dispatch for PJM's Regional Transmission Expansion Plan to determine the economic benefits of transmission projects.

why_it_supports_the_claim: The Missouri PSC technical appendix for a transmission program in MISO territory states that MISO itself performed the techno-economic analysis using PROMOD, based on MISO's own LRTP Tranche 1 data and Future 1 scenario.
notes: Third-party (regulator) attribution of MISO's own process rather than a MISO first-party document; MISO's LRTP Tranche 1 report would be the first-party source for a second look, hence candidate. MISO is already in the catalogue as a PLEXOS user; this is a separate PROMOD record. Also found as: NA-D2-0068; NA-D2-0062; NA-D2-0061; NA-D2-0082.

use_case: ERCOT commissioned Aurora Energy Research to model ERCOT's resource-adequacy needs under the status-quo energy-only market design (two demand scenarios, normal and extreme weather years) and to assess the reliability and system-cost impacts of market-design changes, including variants of the Dispatchable Reliability Reserve Service (DRRS) as an ancillary service and an extended Operating Reserve Demand Curve (ORDC) with a $5,000/MWh offer cap, for a November 2025 report delivered to ERCOT and reviewed at a PUCT open meeting.
source_title: Assessment of Resource Adequacy Needs in ERCOT and Impact of Market Design Changes
exact_snippet_or_quote: This report, prepared for the Electric Reliability Council of Texas, provides an assessment of resource adequacy needs in the ERCOT power market and the impact of market design changes on key reliability and system costs metrics.
why_it_supports_the_claim: A report hosted on ercot.com and explicitly 'prepared for the Electric Reliability Council of Texas' by Aurora Energy Research documents ERCOT commissioning Aurora's dispatch/capacity-expansion model to evaluate resource adequacy and market-design (DRRS/ORDC) options, which is the US use of the tool the task labels Bid3.
notes: TOOL-IDENTITY CAVEAT (reviewer must resolve): the task pairs 'Bid3' with '(Aurora Energy Research)', but my searches show BID3 is actually AFRY's (ex-Poyry) long-term planning tool deployed mainly by European TSOs (e.g. NESO/National Grid ESO, Finland, Denmark), while Aurora Energy Research's model is named 'Aurora' and is, per a Kroll M&A report, 'only deployed in the U.S. market.' This row therefore records the US use of Aurora Energy Research's 'Aurora' dispatch model under the task's 'Bid3' label. The underlying fact (ERCOT using Aurora Energy Research's model) is solid and first-party; the match to the literal string 'Bid3' is not, hence status=candidate. CORROBORATION (also first-party, ERCOT-hosted): https://www.ercot.com/files/docs/2025-12-17/20251217-Aurora-Energy-Research-Report-Workshop.pdf - 'In 2025, ERCOT engaged Aurora Energy Research to perform analysis of potential future resource adequacy conditions and the impact of different market design options, including variations of the Dispatchable Reliability Reserve Service (DRRS).' tool_explicitly_named=false because the evidence names the company 'Aurora Energy Research' (and its model 'Aurora'), not the string 'Bid3'. A separate Aurora Energy Research report for the Texas Association of Business on limiting solar/wind in ERCOT (cms-production.auroraer.com, 2025-04) shows the same tool in US use but that commissioner is a trade body, not a US ISO, so not recorded here.

exact_snippet_or_quote: pypsa_canada is a workflow-based modeling framework for power system analysis in Canada, built on top of PyPSA (Python for Power System Analysis). This tool enables comprehensive energy system optimization and planning for Canadian electricity grids.
why_it_supports_the_claim: The repository is owned by the NRCan GitHub organization and its first-party README describes a PyPSA-based framework for Canadian power system analysis.

summary: Used PyPSA to build PyPSA-Canada, informing analysis of Canadian power system scenarios including the Atlantic Loop.

use_case: PSR's SDDP algorithm (paired with the OptGen capital expansion module) solves the stochastic operating module of Manitoba Hydro's mid-term planning, evaluating multistage investment and operating trade-offs under stochastic hydrothermal operation.
source_title: MEED/MH I-22a-p (U) - Mid-Term Energy and Electric Demand (MEED-22) report, Manitoba Hydro IRP regulatory review
exact_snippet_or_quote: The operating module calculates the stochastic policy that minimizes the average operating costs over the study horizon, considering uncertainties in inflows, renewable generation, equipment failures etc. This problem is solved through the Stochastic Dual Dynamic Programming algorithm (SDDP), developed by PSR. ... 'OptGen 1': uses decomposition techniques allowing the use of SDDP model to incorporate multistage trade-off evaluation considering stochastic hydrothermal operation
why_it_supports_the_claim: Manitoba Hydro's own regulatory filing describes its mid-term planning model as being solved with PSR's SDDP together with the OptGen investment module.
notes: First-party document hosted on Manitoba Hydro's own domain (hydro.mb.ca), in the IRP regulatory review folder.
